senses.gloss: to make an edge, to hem or fringe.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 5:7">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. V, 7</cite> <he>עד שעה שׁיָמוּל</he> until he hems the girdle.
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 5:7">Ib.</cite> <he>ומָל מרוח אחת</he> when he made a hem on one side (of the piece which he cut out of the middle of a piece of cloth).

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 19:4">Sabb. XIX, 4</cite> <he>אחד למול אחר וכ׳</he> one child which was to be circumcised after the Sabbath &c.; <he>ושכח ומָל וכ׳</he> and by mistake he circumcised &c. Ib. 6 <he>מל ולא פרע וכ׳</he> if he circumcised but failed to split the prepuce &c. Ib. 5 (137ᵃ) <he>קטן … אין מוֹלִין</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>מוהלין</he>) a sick infant must not be circumcised.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 25:1">Pesik. R. s. 25</cite> <he>מי מל לשמי וכ׳</he> who circumcised a son in honor of my name, unless I gave him a son?; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 27:2">Lev. R. s. 27</cite> <he>מלל</he> (corr. acc.); a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="M00484"><he>מוּל</he></cite>, pl. <cite ref="M00496"><he>מוּלִים</he></cite>, <he>מוּלִין</he>.

Lev. R. s. 25; Gen. R. s. 46 ומהיכן יִמּוֹל on what part of the body should one be circumcised?—Y. Shebi. IV, end, 35ᶜ משיִמּוֹלוּ from the time they are circumcised. Gen. R. l. c. גזר הרופא שימולו the physician ordered that they must be circumcised; a. fr.—[Polel מוֹלֵל, v. מָלַל.]
